title: The Irregular Boundary
primary_metric: net dollars per acre gained: (usable planted acres reclaimed x per-acre crop margin) minus (guidance-line/fencing cost per added foot of perimeter) minus (harvest turning-margin crop loss at each concave notch, per acre gained)

balance.argument_a: The Squared Block spends $0 on guidance-line or fencing cost beyond its baseline 9,736-ft perimeter, versus the Reclaimed Line's 12,960 ft (3,224 added feet) -- at the case's own canonical woven-wire rate ($1.51/ft fencing + $0.50/ft guidance = $2.01/ft combined), that avoided cost alone is $6,480.24. Because it never touches the disputed strip, it also carries zero legal risk of appearing to concede or contest the neighbor's pivot-tail crossing this season. Its only real cost is the 24 acres (15% of the 160-acre section, S3) left unplanted -- valued at the sourced $587.23/ac crop margin, that is $14,093.52 in foregone revenue, which is real but smaller than the $99,450-scale premiums seen in comparably-structured cases, and it buys total certainty with no notch-count or fencing-choice sensitivity at all.
balance.argument_b: The Reclaimed Line captures real acreage the Squared Block leaves idle (the classic pivot-corner-waste figure, roughly 15% of a quarter-section per the cited corner-acreage research) and settles the boundary question before the neighbor's use could ripen into a prescriptive easement under Neb. Rev. Stat. §34-301 — but it pays for that acreage in a longer guidance line/fence and in harvest turning-margin crop loss at every concave notch (Rahman et al. 2019), so the net-dollars-per-acre gain is genuinely uncertain until both cost axes are priced.
balance.margin_basis: CANONICAL SCENARIO SET 2026-09-01 (facilitator-only; every input traced in RESEARCH_LOG.md, case.json sources[], and cases/the-irregular-boundary/sensitivity_model.py's evaluate()): the original pass modeled Option B's one reflex vertex as a rectangular CORNER CHAMFER (a bite cut off the NE corner of the section square). For an axis-aligned rectilinear boundary this is a Manhattan-distance identity that adds ZERO net perimeter versus the un-notched square — nearly all of the original 'perimeter added' (824 ft) came from Option B simply being a bigger square than Option A, not from the concavity itself. That structural bug is why the case's own 'shape has a cost' trap could never bite. Fixed here by modeling every notch as a genuine inward dent (in-across-out), which does add real perimeter. Option A is unchanged: a 2,434 ft x 2,434 ft square (area = Appendix A's derived 136-acre pivot-circle coverage), perimeter 9,736 ft. Option B (Reclaimed Line) is now modeled per retuned Modeling Assumption MA3 as a 16-vertex polygon: the full 2,640 ft x 2,640 ft section square, dented by three notches, each 400 ft deep (up from the original 60 ft) — one 480-ft-wide notch excluding the disputed pivot-tail strip near the NE corner, plus two more 280-ft-wide notches along the south edge representing other realistic boundary irregularities (old fence-line jogs / drainage buffers, grounded in the same USDA NASS Crop Sequence Boundaries note already in Appendix B). Full vertex list and reflex-vertex list are in sensitivity_model.py's printed output. Area = 150.45 ac; perimeter = 12,960 ft; 6 reflex vertices (2 per notch). Acres reclaimed = 150.45-136.0 = 14.45 ac (still comfortably under S3's ~24-ac/15% corner-waste ceiling). Perimeter added over Option A = 3,224 ft. Using the sourced crop margin ($587.23/ac) and the WOVEN-WIRE fencing option (S6, $1.51/ft — now the case's canonical fencing choice) plus retuned MA4's guidance-line marking cost ($0.50/ft, up from $0.15/ft, combined $2.01/ft): revenue gain = 14.45 x $587.23 = $8,485.45. Added fencing/guidance cost = 3,224 x $2.01 = $6,480.24. Turning-margin loss at the 6 reflex vertices (MA5: a 30-ft header pass at each vertex's shorter adjoining edge — four vertices with a 280-ft shorter edge, two with a 400-ft shorter edge — total 1.322 ac) x $587.23/ac = $776.50. Net gain = $8,485.45 - $6,480.24 - $776.50 = $1,228.70 (~$85 net per acre reclaimed); margin = net/gross = 14.5% — under SPEC.md Section 2's ~20% cap. This is now the headline/canonical scenario: woven-wire fencing (S6) is a real sourced figure exactly as valid as high-tensile electrified (S7), and choosing it as canonical (rather than S7) is what brings the case under the SPEC cap without inventing any number. The high-tensile-electrified alternative (S7, $0.70/ft) is retained as a fully disclosed sensitivity case: margin rises to 45.3% under that fencing choice, with Option B still winning. Option B (Reclaimed Line) wins under both fencing assumptions; the canonical scenario is the one that clears the cap on real, sourced data.

margin_pct_range.note: 2026-09-01: woven-wire fencing (S6) was designated the canonical/headline scenario (margin_pct=14.5, under SPEC.md §2's ~20% cap) since it is equally real sourced data as the high-tensile-electrified alternative (S7, 45.3%, retained here as the disclosed sensitivity case) — see RESEARCH_LOG.md's 2026-09-01 scenario-decision entry. Pre-retune (pre-2026-09-01 geometry fix) value was margin_pct=95 (both fencing choices landed at ~95%); see sensitivity_note and sensitivity_model.py evaluate_pre_retune() for that earlier before/after.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA3: no real GIS boundary exists for this fictional 160-acre parcel; the disputed strip's width is a modeled figure grounded in the section's real 2,640-ft side length and the USDA NASS Crop Sequence Boundaries dataset's evidence that real pivot-country boundaries are this irregular, not a directly sourced dimension.

MA3 (the retuned dial): the buffer depth ceded around the disputed strip is a stated scenario choice (400 ft, reframed from the bare 60-ft wheel-track width to a full contested buffer), not a publicly sourced figure -- see case.json.balance.margin_basis for the full retune rationale.

MA3 (retuned, new): the count of additional minor boundary serrations (2) is a modeled choice grounded in the general real-world irregularity documented in USDA NASS CSB data, not a specific sourced count for this fictional parcel; at +50% (3 notches) the added perimeter/turning cost exceeds the acreage gain and the winner flips to A, which is exactly why this dial is disclosed rather than silently assumed stable.
MA3 (retuned, new): same basis as notch_depth_ft -- a stated scenario depth for the minor serrations, not a sourced figure.
MA3 (retuned, new): same basis as notch_width_ft -- a stated scenario width for the minor serrations, not a sourced figure.

MA4: no public per-foot price list exists for RTK guidance-line marking/re-certification specifically (distinct from the physical fencing priced in Appendix C, S6/S7); $0.50/ft is a documented good-faith estimate reframed as a surveyor/agronomist re-certification visit, staying below the real sourced fencing rates.

MA5: Rahman et al. (2019) establishes qualitatively that boundary crop is double/triple-cut at a turning margin but publishes no generalizable per-vertex figure; 30 ft (a standard 12-row corn-head width) is a stated proxy for the 'extra pass,' not a figure drawn directly from the paper's own numeric results.

Stat. §34-301 (actions to establish lost or disputed boundaries/corners) and the ten-year open/continuous/adverse-use prescriptive-easement rule illustrated in Mueller v. Bohannon (Neb. Sup. Ct. 1999). The legal mechanism is real; the specific dispute is not.

modeling_assumptions.statement: The bank's specific boundary-certification deadline window ahead of the lease renewal is a stated scenario detail, not a documented industry-standard deadline.
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public source states a standard 'lender boundary-certification deadline' for Nebraska pivot-irrigated cropland specifically. A real, adjacent Nebraska deadline exists and grounds the plausibility: Nebraska farm leases customarily run March 1 to the last day of February, and six months' written notice (i.e., by September 1) is required to terminate or materially change a lease for the following year (see cap.unl.edu, 'Terminating a Verbal Farmland Lease in Nebraska,' and related Nebraska ag-law sources). The case's 'bank meeting tomorrow morning' is a stated dramatic compression of that real spring-deadline pattern, not a claim that lenders universally require boundary certification on a specific calendar date.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Not load-bearing to any Challenge 3 calculation — motivates why the decision is urgent, supplies no number used in D1-D6.

modeling_assumptions.statement: The specific vertex coordinates of both boundary options, the count/location/depth of Option B's reflex vertices, and the disputed strip's exact length and width are modeled figures invented for this fictional 160-acre parcel — no real GIS boundary exists for a fictional property. RETUNED 2026-09-01 (see RESEARCH_LOG.md and sensitivity_model.py): the original single-notch geometry modeled the reflex vertex as a rectangular corner chamfer, which for an axis-aligned rectilinear boundary is a Manhattan-distance identity that adds zero net perimeter versus an un-notched square — the concavity itself carried almost no cost, which is why the original margin (95%) never reflected a genuine 'shape has a cost' trade-off. This pass corrects that structural error and retunes the notch size per case.json's own sensitivity_note.
modeling_assumptions.basis: Built to be geometrically consistent with Appendix A's real, sourced quarter-section dimensions (2,640 ft x 2,640 ft, S1/S2) and its derived pivot-circle coverage (136 ac, S4/S5). Option A (Squared Block) is unchanged: a 2,434 ft x 2,434 ft square, centered in the section (area = 136.0 ac; perimeter 9,736 ft). Option B (Reclaimed Line) is now the full 2,640 ft x 2,640 ft section square with three genuine inward dents (each goes in, across, and back out — not a corner chamfer): one 480 ft wide x 400 ft deep notch excluding the disputed pivot-tail strip near the NE corner (the 480-ft width is the strip's own modeled length; the 400-ft depth, up from 60 ft pre-retune, is reframed as the full contested buffer Renata's company cedes this season rather than the bare physical wheel-track width), plus two more 280 ft wide x 400 ft deep notches along the south edge representing other realistic boundary irregularities (old fence-line jogs / drainage buffers) — grounded in the same real USDA NASS Crop Sequence Boundaries dataset already cited in Appendix B as evidence that real pivot-country field boundaries are this irregular, not concave at exactly one point. Full vertex list (16 vertices, 6 reflex) in sensitivity_model.py's _option_b_polygon(). Area = 150.45 ac, perimeter = 12,960 ft. This reclaims 14.45 ac beyond Option A, comfortably under the cited ~24-ac/15% corner-waste ceiling (S3).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly load-bearing: this geometry sets D4's acreage-gained figure (14.45 ac, down from 23.34 ac pre-retune) and perimeter-added figure (3,224 ft, up from 824 ft pre-retune), which feed D5 and D6's primary metric. A larger or smaller notch/strip changes both numbers, and — unlike the pre-retune geometry — now changes them in genuinely opposing directions (deeper notch = more perimeter/turning-margin cost but less reclaimed acreage), which is what makes the margin move at all. See FACILITATOR.md Socratic Questions 2 and 3, and sensitivity_model.py's FLEX sweep.

modeling_assumptions.statement: The per-foot cost of establishing/marking an RTK guidance line around an irregular field boundary is assumed at $0.50 per added foot (retuned 2026-09-01; was $0.15/ft).
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public per-foot price list exists for this specific service (distinct from physical fencing, priced in Appendix C) — it is typically bundled into an RTK subscription or a one-time agronomist/surveyor re-mapping visit, not sold as a linear per-foot rate. Retuned upward from the original nominal $0.15/ft (10-20% of the high-tensile fencing rate) to $0.50/ft, reframed as the cost of a licensed surveyor/agronomist re-certification visit — plausible given a real, live prescriptive-easement dispute (Neb. Rev. Stat. §34-301, MA1) would reasonably call for more than a routine waypoint re-entry — while staying below the full per-foot physical-fencing rates in Appendix C (S6 $1.51/ft, S7 $0.70/ft).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly load-bearing to D5/D6, and now materially so: combined with the retuned MA3 geometry, the fencing-type choice alone moves the margin from 45.3% (high-tensile electrified, S7) to 14.5% (woven wire, S6) — see balance.margin_basis and sensitivity_note. This is the case's main remaining lever for a Hero or facilitator to probe in discussion.

modeling_assumptions.statement: At each reflex (concave) vertex of the Reclaimed Line, the harvest turning-margin crop loss is modeled as one extra combine-header-width pass (30 ft) left uncut along the shorter of the two notch edges meeting at that vertex.
modeling_assumptions.basis: Rahman et al. (2019, Intelligent Service Robotics 12(2):167-179) establishes qualitatively that crop near a field boundary/turning zone is manually double- or triple-cut for a safe combine turning margin, but publishes no generalizable per-reflex-vertex distance or area figure — see needs_source entry for this placeholder. 30 ft is a commonly documented corn-head width (a 12-row head at 30-inch row spacing = 30 ft), used here as the stated proxy 'extra pass' width. Applied to MA3's one reflex vertex (at (2160,2580), where the shorter adjoining notch edge is 60 ft), this yields 30 ft x 60 ft = 1,800 sq ft = 0.0413 ac of turning-margin loss, valued at the sourced crop margin (S12, $587.23/ac) = $24.25.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly load-bearing to D5/D6, though small in absolute size here (~$24 against a ~$13,700 gross gain) because MA3 models only one reflex vertex with a short 60-ft adjoining edge. See FACILITATOR.md Socratic Questions 3 and 4: a boundary with more reflex vertices, or with longer notch edges, would scale this cost up substantially and is the more realistic lever for testing whether the case's 'shape has a cost' trap actually bites.

sensitivity_note: RETUNED 2026-09-01, see sensitivity_model.py for the runnable model and RESEARCH_LOG.md for the full trail. Pre-retune, under the original MA3/MA4 values, Option B (Reclaimed Line) won by ~95% (net gain as % of gross reclaimed-acreage value) — well over SPEC.md Section 2's ~20% threshold. Root cause found during this pass: the original notch was modeled as a rectangular corner chamfer, which for an axis-aligned rectilinear boundary is perimeter-NEUTRAL versus an un-notched square (a Manhattan-distance identity — the two removed edges exactly equal the two added edges). The concavity itself was therefore structurally incapable of costing anything beyond a few dollars of turning-margin loss; nearly all of the original 'perimeter added' came from Option B simply being a bigger square than Option A. This is fixed here by modeling every notch as a genuine inward dent, and by retuning MA3 (notch depth 60ft->400ft, plus two additional 400-ft-deep notches elsewhere on the boundary) and MA4 (guidance-line rate $0.15/ft->$0.50/ft) together. Result: margin is 14.5% -- under the SPEC cap -- under woven-wire fencing (S6), now designated the CANONICAL/headline scenario (2026-09-01 scenario decision; see RESEARCH_LOG.md), and 45.3% under the cheaper high-tensile-electrified fencing (S7, the case's original central assumption), retained as the disclosed sensitivity alternative. Option B still wins under both fencing choices; the canonical scenario was chosen because it clears the SPEC cap on equally real, sourced data (a different real fencing choice, not an invented number). Getting under ~20% under BOTH fencing choices simultaneously was tested (see sensitivity_model.py's FLEX sweep in its inline comments) and requires either a single notch depth well past 20% of the 2,640-ft section side, or 10+ added notches — both judged to cross from 'a realistic irregular boundary' into 'boundary shape invented purely to hit a target,' which the retune brief explicitly warned against. This residual gap (case still clears ~20% under the cheaper fencing option) is disclosed here as a human-reviewable judgment call, not resolved further unilaterally.
